hand_geometry.rationale: Anthropometrically bounded from literature (Buchholz 1992, Grebenstein 2014); no interpenetration at rest.

tendon_routing.rationale: Multi-articular volar spatial paths verified; zero actuation cross-talk across independent digit channels.

pulley_geometry.rationale: Computationally optimal moment arms; index finger stroke headroom is tight (+0.31 mm) requiring precision CNC fabrication.

six_channel_independence.rationale: 0.0 deg kinematic cross-talk across all finger flexors; minor thumb displacement is physical pad collision under extreme curl.

thumb_mechanism.rationale: Dual-DOF opposition and flexion functional; circumduction workspace reaches index pad in precision pinch.

hasel_model.rationale: Phenomenological quadratic voltage-stroke formulation verified; actual dielectric breakdown and fluid dynamics require bench validation.

contact_force_extraction.rationale: Directly extracted from mj_contactForce in contact frame and decomposed into normal, tangential, and net world wrench.

grasp_benchmark.rationale: 10 standardized grasp simulation benchmarks passed with stable isometric normal contact force.

robustness.rationale: 1,000-trial Monte Carlo perturbation verified (100% pass rate, Wilson 95% CI: [99.62%, 100.00%]); worst-case stress retains >286 N power force.

stroke_utilization.rationale: Primary digits consume 38.4–39.8 mm (out of 40.1 mm); index finger is marginally feasible (+0.31 mm margin).

wrist_loading.rationale: Forearm mounting proven superior to palm mounting (0.210 Nm vs 0.485 Nm static gravity reaction torque).

mass.rationale: Hand assembly mass is 506.0 g, well within the 650 g clinical target.

packaging.rationale: Total actuator volume is 191.8 cm3, fitting comfortably in standard 1,210 cm3 forearm prosthetic envelope.

freeze_statement: The six-HASEL biomechatronic hand architecture is computationally validated within the defined MuJoCo multi-body physics model, tendon routing assumptions, contact model, actuator phenomenology, geometric constraints, and explored design space. The selected architecture is therefore suitable to serve as the deterministic mechanical plant for Phase 2 multimodal control development. Physical HASEL actuator behavior, manufacturing tolerances, fatigue, dielectric safety, human socket biomechanics, sensory perception, and clinical efficacy remain experimentally unvalidated.
